headline: Nowhere to sleep tonight
cues: It's ten at night in Blacksburg, and someone has just realised they have nowhere safe to sleep.
Searching dozens of websites is the last thing they should have to do right now.
Today, we'll see how Clear House turns that search into one clear next step.

headline: How Clear House works
title: How does one site find you a home?
cues: Here's our question for today: how can one website find real housing help, fast, without making things up?
We'll go in five steps, from the problem itself to the AI that answers.

headline: What cost burdened means
meaning: A household that spends more than 30 percent of its income on housing.
example: Rent of $1,500 on $4,000 a month is 37.5 percent.
cues: Housing experts call a household cost burdened when housing takes more than thirty percent of its income.
Pay fifteen hundred dollars in rent on four thousand a month, and that's already thirty-seven and a half percent.
When money is that tight, every wrong step costs more.

headline: Help is scattered
cues: Shelters, rent help and affordable homes live on many different county, city and provider websites.
Some waitlists are closed, some listings are out of date, and scams target people in a hurry.
Clear House puts the checked options in one place, with the next step spelled out.

headline: Can't I just walk in?
line: Many shelters start with a phone call.
cues: Most people think a shelter is somewhere you simply walk into.
But many Northern Virginia shelters start with a call to an intake or referral line, which screens you and finds a bed.
So the most useful thing we can show is exactly who to call, and when.

headline: Every record checked by hand
label: CHECKED RESOURCES
cues: Underneath everything is a list of four hundred and nine resources, each checked against an official page.
That's three hundred and nine homes and floor plans, thirty-three emergency shelters and thirty-one help programs.
They cover two regions: Northern Virginia, and Blacksburg near Virginia Tech.

headline: From official page to listing
cues: Each record starts on an official provider or government page, never a search summary.
Phone numbers, addresses and rents are copied exactly, and anything unpublished is marked unknown, not guessed.
Every link says where it really goes, and every listing gets a date when it must be checked again.

headline: Listings expire on purpose
events: Stay listed as call to confirm
cues: A listing that was true last month can quietly stop being true.
So homes drop out of search when their review date passes, about a week after they were checked.
Shelters never disappear for that reason; they simply go back to call to confirm.

headline: What does a county list prove?
question: A home appears on a county affordable-housing list. What does that prove?
choices: The program exists and is official
cues: Quick check: if a home appears on a county list, what does that actually prove?
Think about it.
It proves the program is real and official, not that a unit is free today, so we say call to confirm.

headline: Search the way you live
image_prompt: A flat map of a city with blue house pins, a highlighted office building and a route line to the nearest homes
caption: Near my office at 1800 Tysons Blvd
cues: People don't think in counties; they think about work, school and the bus home.
So you can simply type: a place near my office at eighteen hundred Tysons Boulevard.

headline: Near my office, in seconds
cues: A small script reads the place out of your sentence, and Google Places finds it on the map.
Checked homes are ranked by distance, and Google Routes adds real drive and transit times.
That whole answer arrives almost instantly, because it doesn't need an AI to guess.

headline: Closest homes to Reston Town Center
title: Distance from Reston Town Center
cues: Here's a real answer from our tests for homes near Reston Town Center.
The closest checked home is three tenths of a mile away, about three minutes by car and seven by transit.

headline: A map that follows you
b: A friend pointing at the right street
mapping: When the chat names places or you change a filter, the map moves to show exactly those homes.
cues: The map works like a friend pointing at the right street while you talk.
When an answer names five homes, or you pick a neighbourhood like Reston, the map moves to show exactly those.

headline: Meet Gemma 4
label: GEMMA 4 26B
cues: For open questions, like how to qualify for a voucher, Clear House uses Gemma 4, Google's open model.
Specifically the twenty-six billion parameter version, and every answer says which model wrote it.

headline: Grounding
meaning: Making an AI answer only from facts you give it, not from memory.
example: Gemma sees about a dozen checked records per question.
cues: The key idea is grounding: the AI may only answer from facts we hand it.
A script picks the dozen or so checked records that match your question, and Gemma writes from those alone.

headline: From question to answer
cues: Your question goes in, and the matching records are ranked so the most useful ones come first.
Gemma's answer streams in word by word, and a script turns every named place into a linked card.

headline: Thinking took over a minute
title: Time to the first word of an answer (measured)
cues: On the hosted API, Gemma spent about seventy-two seconds reasoning before writing a single word.
That's far too long for someone looking for shelter tonight.
On our own GPU, the first words arrive in about three seconds.

headline: Our own Gemma on Google Cloud
cues: So we run the very same Gemma 4 model ourselves, on a Cloud Run service with an NVIDIA L4 GPU.
We switch off the long reasoning step, and the GPU sleeps when nobody is using it.
If it's asleep or busy, the site quietly falls back to the Gemini API, so the chat never breaks.

headline: Every piece has a job
image_prompt: Five connected flat blocks: Gemma 4, Cloud Run, Maps Places and Routes, Cloud Build, Secret Manager, linked by lines to a house
caption: Gemma 4 · Cloud Run · Places + Routes · Cloud Build · Secret Manager
cues: Gemma writes the answers, Cloud Run hosts the site and the GPU, and Google Maps finds places and commute times.
Cloud Build packages every release, and Secret Manager keeps the keys out of the code.

headline: Safety comes first
cues: In an emergency, every page leads with nine one one and two one one, before any AI answer.
And Clear House never claims a bed is free; shelters always say call to confirm a bed tonight.

headline: Collect only what we need
cues: There are no accounts, and Social Security and account numbers are removed before any text reaches the AI.
If you tap Near me, your location is rounded to about a hundred metres and never stored.
Domestic violence shelters never show an address, only the hotline to call.

headline: When rent isn't published
cues: Many homes don't publish their rent, and a chatbot could easily invent one.
Instead, Clear House shows a clearly labeled estimate from similar checked homes nearby, and tells you to ask the provider.

headline: If the AI can't answer
question: Gemma doesn't answer in time. What does the person see?
cues: Last check: what happens if Gemma can't answer in time?
Think about it.
The chat still lists the checked resources that match, with phone numbers, so nobody is left with nothing.

headline: What you can now explain
items: Places and Routes for real commute times
Gemma 4 on a Cloud Run GPU, grounded and fast
Safe, private and honest by design
final: A clearer path to a place to call home.
cues: So: four hundred and nine checked resources, maps that think like you, and Gemma 4 answering in seconds on Google Cloud.
All of it grounded, private and honest about what it doesn't know.
A clearer path to a place to call home.
